words.gloss: altered, abnormal; activity, behaviour (īhā); (section) on the knowing

hindi: अब इसके बाद हम विकृतेहाविज्ञानीय नामक शारीर की व्याख्या करेंगे, यानी विकृत चेष्टा के ज्ञान वाले शारीर की।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the Śārīra (the section on the body) named Vikṛtehāvijñānīya, the knowledge of abnormal activity (vikṛta-īhā).
notes: Stock opening formula (atha ataḥ ... vyākhyāsyāmaḥ). The chapter title is read as vikṛta-īhā-vijñānīya, literally 'what is to be known concerning abnormal activity (or behaviour)'. īhā = activity, effort, behaviour; other readings of the compound are possible. The chapter goes on to give signs of approaching death. A closing 'iti' or colophon is not in this unit.

hindi: जो — आकाश मानो ठोस हो गया हो, और जो ठोस है वह मानो आकाश हो — अमूर्त मानो मूर्त हो, और मूर्त; अथवा मूर्त जो अमूर्त अवस्था में स्थित हो —
english: He who — the sky as if it had become solid, and the solid as if it were the sky — The formless as if formed, and the formed; or the formed standing in a formless state —

text_flags.why: possible: 'iva' + 'ākāśam' should join as 'ivākāśam' (a+ā), and the printed run-together form leaves the hiatus unresolved; probably only a print habit of joining words without sandhi
possible: a + a gives long ā (amūrta-avasthita = amūrtāvasthita); printed with short a; the sense is unaffected

notes: [02.10.2] ELLIPTICAL: the verb 'paśyati' (sees) is not in this unit; it occurs in unit 7 ('yaḥ paśyati sa naśyati'). GROUPING: units 2-7 appear to form one sentence (a list of things wrongly seen, with the verb and result in unit 7). Reading: 'ākāśam iva yo ghanam' = the solid (ghana) as if it were sky; 'ghanībhūtam ivākāśam' = sky as if grown solid. The translation supplies no verb. [02.10.3] Continues the list of wrongly seen things (see GROUPING in unit 2). The pairing is ambiguous: 'amūrtam iva mūrtam ca' can be read 'the formless as if formed' or 'the formed as if formless' (compare 'ākāśam iva yo ghanam' in unit 2, where the item compared comes first); the translation follows the word order and does not decide. The second 'mūrtam' repeats the first; 'amūrtāvasthitam' could also be 'amūrte avasthitam'. Medium confidence for that reason.

hindi: तेजस्वी, तेजहीन, और उसी प्रकार; श्वेत, काला, और असत्, सत् आँख के रोग से रहित, और बहुत रूपों वाला, चिह्नरहित चन्द्रमा —
english: The bright (as) lightless, and likewise; the white (as) black, and the unreal (as) real One free from eye disease, and the moon of many forms, without its mark —
notes: [02.10.4] Continues the list of wrongly seen things. The words are bare pairs (bright / lightless / likewise; white / black; unreal / real); '(as)' is carried from 'iva' of unit 3 and is an interpretation, since the Sanskrit states no verb or 'iva' here. 'tadvat' (likewise) probably means the reverse pair also (the lightless as bright), but it is not spelled out. See GROUPING in unit 2. [02.10.5] Continues the list of things seen (see GROUPING in unit 2): the man is free from eye disease (so the sight is not explained by a known eye ailment), and the moon is seen with many forms and without its mark (lāñchana). 'Without mark' probably means without its dark patch; the Sanskrit says only 'mark'. Splitting 'bahurūpam alāñchanam' is preferred to 'bahurūpa-mala-añchana'. Verb 'paśyati' only in unit 7.

words.gram: f. nom. sg. (as printed; acc. vyākṛtim expected)

hindi: जागते हुए राक्षसों, गन्धर्वों, प्रेतों और वैसे ही दूसरों को — रूप, विकृत आकार, और वैसे ही; जो देखता है, वह नष्ट हो जाता है।
english: While awake, demons (rakṣas), gandharvas, pretas (spirits of the dead), and others of that kind — A form, an altered shape (vyākṛti), and likewise — he who sees (these) perishes.

text_flags.why: possible: 'vyākṛti' is an unusual word; 'vikṛti' (deformity, abnormal appearance) is the commoner word, but 'vyākṛti' (altered or distorted shape) also gives sense, so no change is made; also the printed form lacks the final -m of an accusative (vyākṛtim expected), so a dropped anusvāra is possible

notes: [02.10.6] Continues the list of things wrongly seen (unit 2). 'jāgrat' = 'while awake'. rakṣas = demon-beings, gandharva = a class of celestial beings, preta = spirit of the dead; no further identification is made. [02.10.7] Completes the sentence begun in unit 2 (GROUPING: units 2-7 appear to form one sentence; 'yaḥ paśyati sa naśyati' gives the verb and the result). 'rūpam vyākṛti' might be one phrase ('form, an altered shape') or two nouns; '(these)' in the English is the only supplied word and stands for the objects of units 2-6. naśyati = perishes, is lost, dies.
lines_deva: रूपं व्याकृति तद्वच्च यः पश्यति स नश्यति
lines_iast: rūpaṃ vyākṛti tadvacca yaḥ paśyati sa naśyati

words.gloss: Arundhatī (a small star near the great sages; probably Alcor)
Dhruva (the fixed one; probably the pole star)

hindi: जो महर्षियों के समीप स्थित अरुन्धती यानी सम्भवतः अलकोर नामक तारे को नहीं देखता, अथवा ध्रुव यानी सम्भवतः उत्तर दिशा में स्थिर दिखने वाले ध्रुवतारे को, या आकाशगंगा को — वह उस वर्ष को नहीं देखता।
english: He who does not see Arundhatī (probably the star Alcor), standing near the great sages, or Dhruva (probably the pole star), or the Ākāśagaṅgā (the Milky Way) — he does not see that year (samā).
notes: [02.10.8] Identifications, once for units 8-9: the 'great sages' (maharṣi) are probably the Seven Sages, the stars of the Great Bear (probable); Arundhatī = the small star Alcor beside Vasiṣṭha (Mizar), probable; dhruva (unit 9) = the pole star, probable; ākāśagaṅgā (unit 9) = the Milky Way, standard. Units 8-9 appear to form one sentence ('yo na paśyati ... na sa paśyati tāṃ samām'). [02.10.9] samā = year; 'he does not see that year' probably means that he will not live out that year (probable); the Sanskrit says only that he does not see it. The reading of 'tāṃ samāṃ' as an adjective phrase ('that equal one') is not preferred. Identifications are given in unit 8. Continues the sentence of unit 8.
lines_deva: ध्रुवमाकाशगंगां वा न स पश्यति तां समां
lines_iast: dhruvamākāśagaṃgāṃ vā na sa paśyati tāṃ samāṃ

words.gram: dvandva of megha-toya-ogha-nirghoṣa, vīṇā, paṇava, veṇu (compound continues)

words.gloss: paṇava (a small drum); flute (veṇu); born of

hindi: बादल और जल-प्रवाह की गर्जना से तथा वीणा, पणव यानी सम्भवतः छोटे ढोल और बाँसुरी से उत्पन्न और जो दूसरे अविद्यमान शब्दों को सुनता है, अथवा विद्यमान शब्दों को भी नहीं —
english: (ones) born of the roar of cloud and flood-water, of the vīṇā (lute), the paṇava (probably a small drum) and the flute, and who hears other sounds, non-existent ones, or not even existing ones —

text_flags.why: probable: as a member of the compound the feminine stem is vīṇā (megha-toya-ogha-nirghoṣa-vīṇā-paṇava-veṇu-jān); the printed short 'vīṇa' is not a stem form. Syllable count is 16 either way (vī-ṇa / vī-ṇā), so metre does not decide; also printed with a space before 'paṇava'
possible: 'asanto' (nom. pl.) does not agree with the accusative 'śabdān'; 'asataḥ' (acc. pl.) is expected before 'na'; the anusvāra looks like a spurious nasal mark

notes: [02.10.10] The noun 'śabdān' (sounds) is in unit 11; '(ones)' stands for it. The long compound is read as 'born of (megha-toya-ogha-nirghoṣa), (vīṇā), (paṇava) and (veṇu)'; 'megha-toya-ogha' could also be 'cloud-water-flood'. paṇava = a small drum (probable), veṇu = bamboo flute. [02.10.11] Continues unit 10. Sense read as: hears sounds that are not there (with unit 10 listing sounds one might hear: cloud, flood, lute, drum, flute) or fails to hear existing ones; the verb for the second half is carried from 'śṛṇoti' (ellipsis) and is not supplied in the translation. Units 10-11 have no result clause here; the sentence appears to continue into 12. Medium confidence because of the emended word.
lines_deva: शृणोत्यन्यांश्च यः शब्दानसंतो न सतोऽपि वा
lines_iast: śṛṇotyanyāṃśca yaḥ śabdānasaṃto na sato'pi vā

words.gloss: by reversal, in the contrary way

hindi: जो दोनों कानों को दबाकर धुकधुका ध्वनि को नहीं सुनता — इसी प्रकार जो गन्ध, रस और स्पर्श को विपर्यय यानी उलटेपन से मानता है,
english: who, having pressed both ears, would not hear the sound dhukadhukā — Likewise, he who takes smells, tastes and touches by reversal (viparyaya, the contrary way),

text_flags.why: probable (near certain): 'vaṃdha' is not a word; 'gandha' fits 'rasa-sparśa' (the three other senses) and unit 14 'dīpagandham'; ga/va confusion in the scan

notes: [02.10.12] dhukadhukā is an onomatopoeic word for a repeated throbbing or thudding sound; the text does not say what produces it, and no modern identification is made (unidentified). The sentence continues as a list of signs. [02.10.13] The correction gandha is certain in sense but is still a change to the printed text. 'viparyayāt' = by reversal or inversion, i.e. he takes a smell, taste or touch as its opposite; the Sanskrit does not say which. manyate = thinks, regards, takes (to be).

hindi: या जो सर्वथा नहीं, और जो दीप की गन्ध को नहीं सूँघता — जिसके लिए विधि से, दोष के लिए, ... रस; मध्य का शब्द छपाई में टूटा हुआ और अस्पष्ट है, इसलिए यह अनुमानित पाठ पर है।
english: or who does not at all, and who does not smell the odour of a lamp — He for whom, by rule (vidhi), for disorder (doṣa), ... the tastes (rasa); the middle word is damaged in print and unclear, so this line is rendered on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: possible: damaged print; 'svāsthyāya avidhinā' (for health, against the rule) would fit the pattern of reversals in units 13-14 (what normally harms or helps is reversed) but this is only a guess, not adopted in the translation

notes: [02.10.14] ELLIPTICAL: the verb of 'sarvaśo vā na yo' is carried from 'manyate' in unit 13 (probably 'or who does not perceive them at all'); the translation supplies none. 'dīpa-gandha' = the smell of a lamp; the text does not say whether a snuffed or burning lamp. Medium-low risk in the first half-line; confidence medium. [02.10.15] DAMAGED PRINT: the printed Devanagari स्वास्थ्येाधाया has the split ो matra (े + ा), so the IAST 'eā' stands for 'o' (svāsthyodhāyā...); the word still cannot be restored with certainty and is kept unsplit as printed. Possible conjecture (not adopted): 'vidhinā yasya doṣāya svāsthyāyāvidhinā rasāḥ' = 'he for whom the tastes (rasa) lead to disorder when used by rule and to health when used against the rule'. Note that the Sanskrit as printed does not say 'used'. Rendered on a conjectural reading; low confidence.
lines_deva: सर्वशो वा न यो यश्च दीपगंधं नजिघ्रति
lines_iast: sarvaśo vā na yo yaśca dīpagaṃdhaṃ najighrati

words.gloss: in the limb, on the body
rule; preceded by, done by rule

hindi: जिसके अंग मानो धूल से ढके हुए हों, यह अनुमानित पाठ पर है, अथवा जो अंग में चोट को नहीं जानता — तीव्र तप के बिना, अथवा विधिपूर्वक योग के बिना,
english: he whose limbs are strewn as if with dust (on a conjectural reading), or who is not aware of a blow on his limb — Without severe austerity (tapas), or yoga done by rule (vidhi-pūrvaka, preceded by the rule),

text_flags.why: possible: 'paṃ śuneva' is not a phrase; pāṃśunā + iva = pāṃśuneva ('as if with dust') suits 'kīrṇāṅgaḥ' (limbs strewn); the printed text has a wrong space and a short a

notes: [02.10.16] The emendation is adopted in the translation, so it is marked 'on a conjectural reading'; 'śunā iva' ('as with a dog') is formally possible but gives no sense. kīrṇa = strewn, scattered, covered; aṅga = limb, body (both are possible). vetti = knows, is aware of. [02.10.17] 'vāvidhipūrvakam' is read vā + vidhipūrvakam ('or yoga according to rule'), which gives the sense that he knows what is beyond the senses without having done the proper practice; vā + avidhipūrvakam ('yoga not done by rule') is also possible from the print, and the sense would then be different. Continues in unit 18. Reviewer: this print writes an avagraha for vā + a- elsewhere (vā'mūrta u3, vā'lpāśī u24), and none here, which supports vā + vidhipūrvakam.
lines_deva: यः पं शुनेव कीर्णांगो योऽंगे घातं न वेत्ति वा
lines_iast: yaḥ paṃ śuneva kīrṇāṃgo yo'ṃge ghātaṃ na vetti vā

hindi: और जो इन्द्रियों से परे को जानता है — उनके मरण का कथन करना चाहिए। जीभ श्याव यानी गहरे साँवले रंग की, मुख दुर्गन्ध वाला, बायीं आँख धँस जाती है —
english: and who knows what is beyond the senses (atīndriya) — of them one should foretell death. The tongue dusky (śyāva), the mouth putrid, the left eye sinks in —
notes: [02.10.18] The agent of 'ādiśet' is not stated (the physician is understood), so 'one' is used. 'teṣām' is plural against the singular 'yaḥ' (a whole class of such persons). Completes the sentence of units 17-18 (appears to be the main clause). [02.10.19] 'jivhā' is a recognised variant of 'jihvā' (orthographic normalisation, recorded once). 'jivhāśyāvā' is read as two words run together, not a compound (the gender agreement is feminine śyāvā). Continues in unit 20 ('yasya taṃ parivarjayet'). No verb 'is' is supplied.

words.gram: pres. part. ni-√kaṣ, m. nom. sg.

hindi: अथवा जिसके सिर पर पक्षी बैठ जाते हैं, उससे बचना चाहिए। जो मानो पैरों को रगड़ता हुआ, ढले हुए कन्धों वाला, इधर-उधर सरकता है —
english: or the one on whose head birds settle — him one should avoid. who creeps about with drooping shoulders, as if rubbing his two feet —
notes: [02.10.20] Completes the relative clause of unit 19 (appears to be one sentence with 19). The agent of 'parivarjayet' is not stated (the physician is understood). līyante = cling to, settle upon; the sense 'hide, melt away' is not intended. 'avoid' (give up as a patient) is the literal sense; the text does not say why. [02.10.21] nikaṣan iva pādau = as if scraping or rubbing the feet (probably against the ground, which is not stated). 'cyutāṃsa' = with fallen (drooping) shoulders.
lines_deva: खगा वा मूर्ध्नि लीयंते यस्य तं परिवर्जयेत्
lines_iast: khagā vā mūrdhni līyaṃte yasya taṃ parivarjayet

hindi: जो हितकर बहुत अन्न खाता हुआ बल से लगातार क्षीण होता जाता है — जो थोड़ा खाता है और जिसके मल और मूत्र बहुत हैं, और जो बहुत खाता है और जिसके मूत्र और मल थोड़े हैं —
english: who, eating much wholesome (hita) food, continually declines in strength — who eats little and has much faeces and urine, and who eats much and has little urine and faeces —
notes: [02.10.22] 'though' in the English translates the sense of the participle 'aśnan' (eating) against the decline; the Sanskrit has only the participle. hīyate = is reduced, wastes. [02.10.23] viṭ = faeces. The final form 'alpa-mūtra-viṭ' is read as bahuvrīhi 'having little urine and faeces'. Continues the list of signs.

hindi: अथवा जो थोड़ा खाने वाला, कफ से पीड़ित, लम्बी साँस लेता है और चेष्टा करता है — जो लम्बी श्वास भीतर लेकर और छोटी श्वास बाहर छोड़कर थक जाता है —
english: or who, eating little and afflicted by Kapha, breathes long and stirs — who, having breathed in long and breathed out short, becomes exhausted —

text_flags.why: probable: 'ucchrasya' is not a verb form; 'ucchvasya' (having breathed in) pairs with 'niśvasya' (having breathed out); v/r confusion in the scan

notes: [02.10.24] ceṣṭate = stirs, moves, makes effort (alternative: struggles); 'and' joining 'śvasiti ceṣṭate' is not in the Sanskrit and is added only for English and Hindi flow. If 'ceṣṭate' is read with 'dīrgham' it could mean 'breathes long when he exerts himself'; the plain list reading is taken. [02.10.25] ucchvasya here = having drawn in a breath (inhaled); niśvasya = having let it out. paritāmyati = is exhausted, faints (the former is the plainer rendering).
lines_deva: यो वाऽल्पाशी कफेनार्तो दीर्घं श्वसिति चेष्टते
lines_iast: yo vā'lpāśī kaphenārto dīrghaṃ śvasiti ceṣṭate

hindi: और जो छोटी साँस लेता है और झटके खाता हुआ अत्यन्त फड़कता है — जो कठिनाई से सिर को इधर-उधर फेंकता है ...; पंक्ति का शेष अंश छपाई में टूटा हुआ और अस्पष्ट है, इसलिए यह अनुमानित पाठ पर है।
english: and who breathes short and throbs violently, jerked about (vyāviddha) — who with difficulty tosses his head about ...; the rest of the line is damaged in print and unclear, so this is rendered on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: probable: a final 'd' of kṛcchrād appears to be lost before 'yo' (kṛcchrāt = with difficulty); the scan drops letters
damaged print: 'acayitvā' and 'prapāṇikau' give no recognisable sense; kept as printed, no guess adopted

notes: [02.10.26] vyāviddham (lit. 'thrown about' or 'pierced through') is taken adverbially, 'in a jerked manner'; other readings: 'with a pierced feeling'. spandate = throbs, quivers, twitches. [02.10.27] DAMAGED PRINT: 'acayitvā prapāṇikau' is kept as printed and is unclear; nothing is built on it. Only 'śiro vikṣipate kṛcchrāt yaḥ' (who with difficulty throws his head about) is secure, and even that is on a conjectural reading because of the damaged end. Low confidence. Reviewer conjecture (not adopted): 'acayitvā' may be 'añcayitvā' (having drawn up/bent, √añc); 'prapāṇikau' stays unrestorable. Low confidence kept.
lines_deva: ह्रस्वं च यः प्रश्वसिति व्याविद्धं स्पंदते भृशं
lines_iast: hrasvaṃ ca yaḥ praśvasiti vyāviddhaṃ spaṃdate bhṛśaṃ

words.gloss: being raised up, being made to stand
words.gram: pres. pass. part. caus. ud-√sthā, m. nom. sg.

hindi: जिसके माथे से पसीना बहता है, और जिसके जोड़ और बन्धन ढीले हैं — जो उठाए जाने पर मोहग्रस्त यानी सम्भवतः मूर्च्छित हो जाता है, बलवान अथवा दुर्बल भी —
english: whose sweat trickles from the forehead, and whose joinings (sandhāna) and bindings (bandhana) are slack — who, when being raised up, would become bewildered (probably faint), whether strong or even weak —
notes: [02.10.28] 'sandhāna-bandhana' is read as 'joinings and bindings' (probably the joints and what binds them); the text gives no more precise anatomical term, so none is supplied. Continues the list of signs. [02.10.29] saṃmuhyet = become confused, lose consciousness (probably fainting; both are possible). The Sanskrit says 'strong or even weak', i.e. whatever his strength.

words.gloss: bed; seat; wall; and so on
wishes to grasp, tries to seize

hindi: जो केवल चित लेटकर सोता है और दोनों पैरों को विकृत करता है — शय्या, आसन, दीवार आदि पर जो अविद्यमान को ही पकड़ना चाहता है —
english: who sleeps only on his back (uttāna, face up) and distorts his two feet — who tries to grasp only what is non-existent, on bed, seat, wall and so on —
notes: [02.10.30] vikaroti = alters, distorts, makes abnormal (alternative: moves about irregularly); the print has 'uttānaeva' with the hiatus unresolved (regular sandhi gives 'uttāna eva'). [02.10.31] jighṛkṣati is desiderative of √grah: wishes to seize, tries to grasp. 'ādau' = in the group beginning with bed, seat and wall (so on).
lines_deva: उत्तानएव स्वपिति यः पादौ विकरोति च
lines_iast: uttānaeva svapiti yaḥ pādau vikaroti ca

words.gloss: not to be laughed at; laughing

words.gram: pres. part. sam-√muh, m. nom. sg.

hindi: जो न हँसने योग्य बात पर हँसता है, मोहग्रस्त होता हुआ, और दोनों दन्तच्छद यानी ओठों को चाटता है — जो ऊपरी ओठ के चारों ओर चाटता है, यह अनुमानित पाठ पर है, और डकारें उत्पन्न करता है —
english: who laughs at what is not to be laughed at, growing bewildered, and licks his two lips (daśana-cchada, lit. tooth-covers) — who licks around his upper lip and makes belches (on a conjectural reading) —

text_flags.why: possible: 'lehanti' is a plural verb and 'lehanty' does not suit the singular 'yaḥ ... karoti'; parilehati (3 sg.) is expected; pe/pa and an extra nasal look like scan errors

notes: [02.10.32] daśanacchada = 'tooth-cover', the lip (standard). 'ahāsya-hāsin' = one who laughs at what is not laughable (alternative: laughs without cause). [02.10.33] The emended verb is adopted in the translation and so is marked 'on a conjectural reading'. udgāra = belch, eructation (standard). 'uttaroṣṭha' = upper lip. Also compare unit 32 'leḍhi' (singular).

words.gloss: physician; medicine; drink; food; elder, teacher (guru); friend; haters

hindi: जिस पर छाया, काली, पीली अथवा लालिमा लिए भी, झपटती है — और जो वैद्य, औषध, पेय, अन्न, गुरु और मित्र से द्वेष करते हैं —
english: whom a shadow rushes at, black, yellow, or even reddish — and those who hate the physician, medicine, drink, food, elders (guru) and friends —
notes: [02.10.34] chāyā = shadow (also 'lustre, colour'; the plainer rendering is kept). abhidravati = rushes at, runs towards (in a hostile or approaching sense is not stated). Continues the list of signs. [02.10.35] GROUPING: the relative clause 'ye' appears to continue into unit 36 (vaśagāḥ sarva eva ete ...), which gives the predicate; this unit is incomplete alone. guru = elder or teacher in this list (not 'heavy'). bhiṣag = bhiṣaj (j becomes g before bh).

words.gloss: Samavartin, 'acting evenly', an epithet of Yama (standard)

hindi: ये सभी समवर्ती यानी यम के वश में गए हुए जानने चाहिए। जिसकी गर्दन, ललाट और हृदय ठंडे होकर पसीजते हैं
english: All these are to be known as gone under the sway of Samavartin (Yama). He whose neck, forehead and heart sweat while cold
notes: [02.10.36] 'ete' refers to signs listed before this unit. Samavartin (literally 'acting evenly') is a standard epithet of Yama (standard); read as genitive singular, 'of Samavartin'. 'sarva eva ete' is printed as one string: sarve eva ete, with the usual e-before-vowel sandhi. [02.10.37] GROUPING: appears to continue in the next unit ('uṣṇo'paraḥ pradeśaś ca ... tasya'). 'śītalam' is neuter singular, agreeing with the neuter dvandva compound. Whether the sweat or the parts are cold is not decided by the Sanskrit.

hindi: और दूसरा प्रदेश यानी भाग गरम है; उसकी शरण देवता हैं। जो सूक्ष्म ज्योति वाला, अनेकाग्र यानी जो एकाग्र यानी एक बिन्दु पर टिका हुआ नहीं है, दुश्छाय यानी बुरी कान्ति वाला और सदा दुर्मना यानी खिन्न मन वाला है।
english: And the other region is hot; his refuge is the deities. He who is of small light (aṇujyotis), not one-pointed in mind (anekāgra), ill-lustred or ill-complexioned (duśchāya), and always low-spirited.
notes: [02.10.38] GROUPING: appears to continue the relative clause of the previous unit ('yasya'). Copula understood in 'uṣṇaḥ aparaḥ pradeśaḥ' and in 'śaraṇaṃ tasya devatāḥ'. 'The other region' is not specified in the text. [02.10.39] 'jyotis' (light) is not specified: eye-light or bodily lustre are both possible. 'anekāgra' is read as an-ekāgra (not one-pointed); aneka-agra (many-pointed) gives the same sense. 'chāyā' can mean lustre, complexion or shadow. The sentence has no main verb here; the relative clause continues in the next unit (appears to).

words.gloss: offering; eaters: bali-eaters (balibhuj, probably crows; probable)

hindi: जिसकी रखी हुई बलि को बलिभुज यानी सम्भवतः कौए नहीं खाते। और जो बिना कारण मेधा यानी बुद्धि, शोभा, उपचय यानी वृद्धि और श्री यानी समृद्धि
english: He whose set-out offering (bali) the bali-eaters (balibhuj, probably crows) do not eat. And he who, without cause, intellect (medhā), beauty (śobhā), growth (upacaya), prosperity (śrī)
notes: [02.10.40] 'balibhuj' literally means 'eater of the bali offering'; the usual dictionary sense is crow (probable); other bali-eating beings are not excluded by the word. 'praṇīta' here taken as 'set out, offered' agreeing with 'balim'. The relative clause 'yasya ...' has its main clause outside this unit. [02.10.41] GROUPING: the verb 'prāpnoti' is in the next unit; the four objects here depend on it. Translation ends where the unit ends.
lines_deva: निर्निमित्तं च यो मेधां शोभामुपचयं श्रियं
lines_iast: nirnimittaṃ ca yo medhāṃ śobhāmupacayaṃ śriyaṃ

hindi: पाता है, अथवा इनसे पतन यानी ह्रास पाता है, वह यम के घर को पहुँचता है। जिस स्वस्थ या रोगी की गुण और दोष से बनी
english: obtains, or from these a falling away (vibhraṃśa); he reaches the abode of Yama. Whose (one) made up of guṇa (quality) and doṣa, of a healthy or of an ill person
notes: [02.10.42] GROUPING: completes the sentence begun in the previous unit (appears to). 'ato vā' is ambiguous (from these, or 'from this cause'); read as 'or, from these, a falling away': the sense is a sudden gain or a sudden loss without cause. 'kṣaya' is masculine 'abode'. [02.10.43] GROUPING: the noun 'prakṛtiḥ' (agreeing with 'mayī') and its verb are in the next unit. 'guṇa' is kept as the doctrinal term; it is not specified further here. Elliptical: translation ends with the unit.

hindi: प्रकृति यानी स्वाभाविक अवस्था बदल जाती है; अनुमानित पाठ पर, वह छह मास तक जीवित नहीं रहता। भक्ति, शील, स्मृति, त्याग, बुद्धि और बल, बिना कारण
english: The natural state (prakṛti) goes into change; on a conjectural reading, he does not live six months. Devotion (bhakti), character (śīla), memory (smṛti), giving up (tyāga), intellect (buddhi) and strength (bala), without cause.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ṣaṇmāsānta' is not a grammatical form (antaḥ/antam/ante); 'ṣaṇmāsān na sa jīvati' ('he does not live six months') gives a regular form and fits the signs that follow; syllable count is the same (16) either way

notes: [02.10.44] Emendation is conjectural. As printed, 'ṣaṇmāsānta sa jīvati' would read 'he lives to the end of six months' (another possible repair is 'ṣaṇmāsānte'); the two sense-options differ (he lives up to six months, or not even six). GROUPING: continues 43 (subject 'prakṛtiḥ' with 'yasya ... guṇadoṣamayī'); the sentence is 'whose prakṛti ... changes, he ...'. Reviewer: ta/na is a known OCR confusion in this print, so 'ṣaṇmāsānta sa' may be 'ṣaṇmāsānna sa' (one letter); this favours 'ṣaṇmāsān na' but is not proof. OPEN for owner: 'does not live six months' vs 'lives to the end of six months' (opposite senses). [02.10.45] GROUPING: appears to continue in the next unit; 'ahetukam' (without cause) probably belongs with the verb 'nivartante' there. The object of 'bhakti' is not stated. 'tyāga' may be read 'generosity' as well as 'giving up'.

hindi: ये छह, छह मास में मरने वाले से हट जाते हैं। अनुमानित पाठ पर: मतवाले के समान चाल, वाणी, कम्पन और मोह, एक मास में मरने वाले के।
english: These six turn away from one who will die in six months. On a conjectural reading: gait, speech, trembling and bewilderment like those of a drunk man, in one who will die in a month.

text_flags.why: possible: 'gāti' is not a standard word for 'gait'; 'gati' (going, gait) fits the drunk comparison; the sense is unaffected

notes: [02.10.46] Completes 45 (appears to): the six are bhakti, śīla, smṛti, tyāga, buddhi, bala. 'ṣaḍbhir māsaiḥ' is an instrumental of time, 'in six months'. [02.10.47] 'māsān' is māsāt (ablative of time) before m. Whether 'mattavat' qualifies only gait and speech or all four items is not decided. Elliptical: no verb. Reviewer: 'gātra' (limb/body) for printed 'gāti' is an equally short repair (gātra-vāk-kampa-mohāḥ); not decidable from the print.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर: नष्ट होता है; शब्द अज्ञाननूषड्हात् अस्पष्ट है; केश नोचने की पीड़ा। और जिसका आहार गले तक नहीं जाता, गले के रोग के सिवा
english: On a conjectural reading: is lost; the word 'ajñānanūṣaḍhāt' is unclear; the pain of hair-plucking. And he whose food does not go to the throat (kaṇṭha), except for a throat ailment.

text_flags.why: damaged print: the whole line is printed as one token with no spaces; 'ajñānanūṣaḍhāt' cannot be restored (one guess only: 'ṣaḍahāt' 'in six days'; 'ajñāna' and 'nū' unexplained); 'vedanām' (accusative) has no verb that takes it, so 'naśyati' may also be wrong

notes: [02.10.48] Damaged. Only 'keśa-luñcana-vedanā' (pain of hair-plucking) is firm. The grammatical frame is unknown, so no verb-object relation is claimed between 'naśyati' and 'vedanām'. [02.10.49] 'ṛte' takes the ablative. The sentence continues with a result beyond this unit (appears to); the translation ends with the unit.
lines_deva: न याति यस्य चाहारः कंठं कंठामयादृते
lines_iast: na yāti yasya cāhāraḥ kaṃṭhaṃ kaṃṭhāmayādṛte

hindi: सेवक विपरीत चलते हैं और प्रेत की आकृति उत्पन्न होती है। जिसकी नींद निरन्तर हो अथवा बिलकुल न हो, वह जीवित नहीं रहता।
english: Servants go contrarily, and the form of a preta (departed spirit, ghost) arises. He whose sleep is constant, or not at all, does not live.
notes: [02.10.50] 'udīryate' is taken as middle 'arises'; the passive 'is uttered/stirred up' is also possible. 'pretākṛti' is read 'the form of a preta'; whose form (the person's) is not stated. [02.10.51] 'naiva vā' is read 'or not at all', so the sleep is either constant or absent.
lines_deva: यस्य निद्राभवेन्नित्या नैव वा न स जीवति
lines_iast: yasya nidrābhavennityā naiva vā na sa jīvati

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर: मुख आँसुओं से भर जाता है और दोनों पैर बहुत पसीजते हैं। और जो यम के राज्य को जाने वाला है उसकी आँख व्याकुलता में पड़ जाती है।
english: On a conjectural reading: the face is filled with tears, and both feet sweat greatly. And the eye of one who will go to the realm of Yama falls into agitation (ākulatā).

text_flags.why: possible: 'vakram' (crooked) gives no sense, 'vaktram' (face) is expected; the half-line has 15 syllables as printed and 16 with 'āpūryate', which also fits the genitive 'aśrūṇām'

notes: [02.10.52] Printed 'ārpyate' (ā-√ṛ caus. pass.) would mean 'is placed / delivered', not 'is filled'; `words` therefore carry the conjectured 'āpūryate' ('is filled'), as in the text_flag. Both 'ārpyate' and 'āpūryate' sit oddly with the genitive 'aśrūṇām' (instrumental expected); the whole repair is conjectural. 'svidyataḥ' is 3rd dual, agreeing with 'caraṇau'. 'vaktra' can be face or mouth. [02.10.53] 'cakṣuścākulatāṃ' is cakṣuḥ ca ākulatām (ś before c; ca + ā). 'ākulatā' = agitation, confusion, disorder.

hindi: जिन भावों में वह पहले रमता है, उनसे अरति वाला वह जीवित नहीं रहता। और वैद्य पूछे जाने पर भी सुनने में कठिन मृत्यु को कहे।
english: Displeased (arati) with those things (bhāva) in which he formerly delighted, he does not live. And the physician, even when asked, should tell the death that is hard to hear.

text_flags.why: possible: two 'ca' in a row is odd; न्न could be misread as च्च in the scan, which would give 'should not tell, even if asked'; NOT adopted here, the printed reading is translated

notes: [02.10.54] 'aratiḥ' is feminine 'displeasure', used as a predicate or adjective of the unstated subject. 'bhāva' = state, thing, object of enjoyment. [02.10.55] The doubled 'ca' is left partly untranslated (the second 'ca' has no clear function). If the intended reading is 'kathayen na ca' the meaning would be the opposite ('should not tell'). GROUPING: 'maraṇam' appears to be completed by the genitives in the next unit. 'kathayet' is 10th-class, not causative.

words.gloss: gone; breath: one whose life-breath is gone
Yama; messenger; piśāca (a class of demon); beginning with

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर: जिसके प्राण चले गए हैं उसके, बन्धुओं और मित्रों के; और उसकी चिकित्सा करने की इच्छा नहीं करनी चाहिए। क्योंकि परासु यानी जिसके प्राण चले गए हैं वह यम के दूतों, पिशाचों आदि द्वारा उपासित होता है यानी उसके निकट रहा जाता है,
english: On a conjectural reading: of one whose life-breath has gone (gatāsu), of kinsmen and friends; and one should not wish to treat him. since one whose life-breath has departed (parāsu) is attended by those beginning with Yama's messengers and piśācas,

text_flags.why: possible: 'icchet taṃ cikitsitam' does not parse naturally; the infinitive 'cikitsitum' ('to treat') is expected after 'icchet'; a final -um misprinted -aṃ is plausible
possible: long ū in '-rūpāsyate' is a print slip for 'parāsur upāsyate'

notes: [02.10.56] 'na cecchet' = na ca icchet (ca + i = e). 'gatāsu' (literally 'whose breath has gone') is used of one who is dying or dead; treatment being discussed, a dying person is probably meant. The genitives 'gatāsoḥ' and 'bandhumitrāṇām' may belong to 'maraṇam' (death) of the previous unit; their exact relation is not certain. The unit as a whole is elliptical. [02.10.57] 'yat' is the conjunction 'since' (gender does not agree with parāsuḥ, m.). 'ādya' = 'beginning with', no 'such as' is supplied. GROUPING: continues in the next unit (appears to).

hindi: औषधों के वीर्य यानी शक्ति को नष्ट करने वालों द्वारा; इसलिए उससे बचना चाहिए। रिष्ट यानी मृत्यु के लक्षण के बिना मृत्यु नहीं है, और जिसमें रिष्ट देखा गया है ऐसा जीवन भी है।
english: by those who destroy the potencies (vīrya) of medicines; therefore one should avoid him. There is no death without riṣṭa (sign of death), and there is life in which riṣṭa has been seen.
notes: [02.10.58] Continues 57 (appears to): 'ghnadbhiḥ' qualifies the instrumentals of 57. Agent of 'parivarjayet' is not stated ('one'). [02.10.59] 'ariṣṭam' is read a-riṣṭa 'without riṣṭa', agreeing with 'maraṇam'; 'dṛṣṭariṣṭam' = dṛṣṭa-riṣṭa (not dṛṣṭa-ariṣṭa, which would show ā). Copula understood in the second clause. Reviewer: ca may carry nāsti into the second clause: 'there is no death without riṣṭa, and no life (in one) in whom riṣṭa has been seen'. This fits u62 (death in riṣṭa is certain) and u60 better than the translation given; OPEN for owner.
lines_deva: अरिष्टं नास्ति मरणं दृष्टरिष्टं च जीवितं
lines_iast: ariṣṭaṃ nāsti maraṇaṃ dṛṣṭariṣṭaṃ ca jīvitaṃ

hindi: जहाँ रिष्ट नहीं है वहाँ रिष्ट का ज्ञान; और रिष्टों में नहीं, निपुणता के अभाव से। यह चरक का वचन है; सुश्रुत के द्वारा तो पढ़ा जाता है।
english: In the absence of riṣṭa, knowledge of riṣṭa; and not in riṣṭas, from lack of skill. This is the statement of Caraka; but by Suśruta it is recited.
notes: [02.10.60] Elliptical (no verb). Probably it means a false recognition of riṣṭa where none exists and a failure to recognise real riṣṭas, both from lack of skill; this is an inference, the Sanskrit does not say 'false' or 'failure'. [02.10.61] 'iti' is read as 'thus, this'. The object of 'paṭhyate' is not stated (the statement of the following unit appears to be meant). Caraka and Suśruta are taken as names of the two authorities.

words.gloss: rasāyana (rejuvenation therapy; standard); austerity; giving; intent on

hindi: क्योंकि रिष्ट होने पर मृत्यु निश्चित है; वह, कहते हैं, निर्मल ब्राह्मणों द्वारा और रसायन यानी पुनर्यौवनकारी चिकित्सा, तप और दान में लगे हुओं द्वारा हटाया जाता है।
english: For death in riṣṭa is certain; that, it is said, by stainless brāhmaṇas and is warded off by those intent on rasāyana (rejuvenation therapy), austerity (tapas) and giving (dāna).
notes: [02.10.62] GROUPING: the verb 'nivāryate' is in the next unit, with the instrumentals continuing there. 'tat' (that) is the neuter subject of the next verb; its referent (death or its certainty) is not stated here. 'dhruvam' could also be adverbial ('surely'). [02.10.63] Completes 62 (appears to): 'tat' of 62 is the subject. 'rasāyana' = rejuvenation therapy (standard).

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर नाम के लिए: कृष्णात्रेय, रिष्ट दो प्रकार का, स्थिर और अस्थिर के भेद से। दोषों की अधिकता से भी रिष्ट का आभास उत्पन्न हो सकता है।
english: On a conjectural reading of the name: Kṛṣṇātreya, riṣṭa twofold, by the division into stable and unstable. Even from an abundance of the doṣas, a semblance of riṣṭa (riṣṭābhāsa) may arise.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kṛṣṇātareya' is not a known name; 'kṛṣṇātreya' (Kṛṣṇa Ātreya) fits, and the half-line has 17 syllables as printed and 16 with the correction

notes: [02.10.64] No verb in the Sanskrit (probably 'says/holds' is understood). The 'twofold' division is stable (sthira) and unstable (asthira) riṣṭa, as taken up in the next units. [02.10.65] 'api' is taken with 'doṣāṇām' ('even from the doṣas'), meaning a riṣṭa-like appearance arises without real riṣṭa.

hindi: उन दोषों के शान्त होने पर शान्त हो जाए; परन्तु स्थायी निश्चय ही मृत्यु के लिए है। आयुर्वेद यानी जीवन के शास्त्र का सम्पूर्ण फल, जो आयु के ज्ञाता में प्रतिष्ठित है।
english: On the subsiding of those doṣas it would subside; but the lasting (one) is certainly for death. The whole fruit of Āyurveda (the science of life), which is established in one who knows lifespan (āyurjña).
notes: [02.10.66] GROUPING: continues 65 (appears to): the unstated subject of 'śāmyet' is the riṣṭābhāsa of 65, and 'sthāyi' stands for the stable riṣṭa of 64. Copula understood in the second clause. 'sthāyi' could be sthāyī (m.) or sthāyi (n.), so no gender is given. [02.10.67] 'yat' is a relative pronoun agreeing with 'phalam' (n.). 'āyurjña' = one who knows the span of life; the main clause is carried by the next unit (appears to).

words.gloss: riṣṭa (sign of death); knowledge; attentive to
abnormal; activity, movement; relating to knowledge

hindi: इसलिए वैद्य को सदा ही रिष्ट के ज्ञान का आदर करने वाला होना चाहिए। इस प्रकार विकृतेहाविज्ञानीय नामक दसवाँ अध्याय।
english: Therefore the physician should always be attentive to the knowledge of riṣṭa. Thus the tenth chapter, named Vikṛtehāvijñānīya.
notes: [02.10.68] 'ādṛta' is taken as active 'regardful, attentive'. The alternative 'honoured for knowledge of riṣṭa' is possible but less natural. [02.10.69] Colophon; the closing 'iti' is 'thus'. The title is kept transliterated; analysed as vikṛta-īhā-vijñānīya it probably means 'relating to knowledge of abnormal activities', not applied in the translation.
